text:
elena: Heads-up — we got a customer escalation from Acme about p95 latency jumping ~3x starting right after the new NVIDIA driver rollout in eu-west-1 at ~02:05 UTC. API errors low, just tail latency.
sam: ack. do we have correlation with kernel/driver deploy window?
elena: yes — infra deploy logs show driver 535.86 rolled to the eu-west pool at 02:03. Acme calls started to spike at 02:08.
mike: grabbing metrics now — looking at host io and nvme qdepth for nodes serving acme replicas. link: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/host-io/eu-west1?orgId=1
anjali: i see KV cache eviction rate up and more remote fetches around same time. could be host-level IO blocking kv cache writes.
elena: customer repro steps attached from support: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/complete -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"model":"gpt-rl-13b","input":"large prompt ~6k chars"}'
```
sam: can we repro locally on a eu-west node? any config differences?
mike: tried a few requests on a canary host with driver 535.86 under load — p95 lifted from 180ms -> 600ms and iowait jumped. I ran `iostat -xz 1` and saw NVMe util ~98% on writes.
anjali: interesting — kernel pagecache flushes spiked. suspect small IO bursts causing host-side backpressure, affects async writes for kv cache and journaling.
elena: support also saw an increase in approx 429-like queuing at our gateway (not auth). it's upstream of model runtime.
infra-oncall: recommended immediate mitigations?
sam: short-term: 1) pin rollback nodes in eu-west to previous driver (534.xx) for acme's dedicated pool, 2) enable routing fallback to older compatible model variant in other region, 3) throttle background maintenance tasks (snapshot, compaction) on impacted hosts.
mike: rolling a targeted rollback for the acme pool now (canary first). deploy-bot: "rollback started for host-pool eu-west-acme (batch 1/4)" :gear:
anjali: also increase KV cache in-memory budget for acme routing to reduce host write pressure — pushing policy change to router.
elena: for longer term, let's capture perf traces: tcpdump + perf + nvme logs for impacted hosts and open a driver/firmware triage with vendor. need reproducer.
sam: repro notes: large prompts + non-cacheable prefixes + concurrent cold-starts amplify the issue. steps: run 50 concurrent requests with 3-6k token prompts, ensure kv cache miss rate >30%.
mike: I've collected a sample trace and put on S3: s3://redwood-prod-traces/4532109999-acme-driver-spike.tar.gz
anjali: actions logged: rollback to 534.21 for acme pool, throttle background jobs, router config bump, trace upload. Monitoring: watch p95, ioutil, kv eviction.
elena: support notified Acme about mitigation and asking for repro payloads. Thanks everyone. follow-ups: create incident postmortem and schedule vendor escalation if rollback confirms improvement. :white_check_mark:
